title: Perimeter and Area of Plane Shapes
seo_title: Perimeter and Area – Primary 6 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find the perimeter and area of squares, rectangles, triangles, parallelograms, trapeziums and composite shapes; solve problems. (summary of the NERDC Primary 6 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 maths worksheets on area: rectangles, triangles, parallelograms, trapeziums and composite shapes, with word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Use the height at right angles to the base.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Area of a rectangle = length × breadth. Area of a parallelogram = base × height.
  • Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height.
  • Area of a trapezium = ½ × (sum of the parallel sides) × height.

Examples

Example

Triangle with base 12 cm and height 7 cm

½ × 12 × 7

Answer: 42 cm²

Example

Trapezium with parallel sides 6 m and 10 m, height 4 m

½ × 16 × 4

Answer: 32 m²

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the slanting side as the heightThe height is at right angles to the base.
Forgetting the ½ for a triangleA triangle is half a parallelogram.
Giving area in cmArea is in square units.

items.q: The dashed line splits the shape into two rectangles. What is the area of the shape?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 7 × 12 = 84 and 8 × 5 = 40. Add: 84 + 40 = 124 cm². Use each part once: 7 × 12 + 15 × 5 = 159 counts the 7 × 5 corner twice.

items.q: The dashed line splits the shape into two rectangles. What is the area of the shape?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 6 × 7 = 42 and 4 × 4 = 16. Add: 42 + 16 = 58 m². Use each part once: 6 × 7 + 10 × 4 = 82 counts the 6 × 4 corner twice.

items.q: What is the area of this compound shape?
items.e: Whole rectangle 12 × 7 = 84, take away the missing corner 5 × 4 = 20: 84 − 20 = 64 cm². Or: split it into two rectangles: 7 × 7 = 49 and 5 × 3 = 15. Add: 49 + 15 = 64 cm².

items.q: What is the area of this compound shape?
items.e: Whole rectangle 10 × 9 = 90, take away the missing corner 6 × 4 = 24: 90 − 24 = 66 m². Or: split it into two rectangles: 4 × 9 = 36 and 6 × 5 = 30. Add: 36 + 30 = 66 m².

items.q: What is the area of this compound shape? Find the two missing lengths first.
items.e: Missing lengths: 14 − 8 = 6 and 11 − 6 = 5. Whole rectangle 14 × 11 = 154, take away the missing corner 6 × 5 = 30: 154 − 30 = 124 cm².

items.q: What is the area of this compound shape? Find the two missing lengths first.
items.e: Missing lengths: 14 − 6 = 8 and 7 − 3 = 4. Whole rectangle 14 × 7 = 98, take away the missing corner 8 × 4 = 32: 98 − 32 = 66 m².

items.q: What is the perimeter of this compound shape?
items.e: Find the missing lengths: 8 − 5 = 3 and 11 − 5 = 6. Then add all 6 sides: 5 + 3 + 6 + 5 + 11 + 8 = 38 m.

items.q: What is the perimeter of this compound shape?
items.e: Find the missing lengths: 6 + 9 = 15 and 6 + 4 = 10. Then add all 6 sides: 6 + 6 + 9 + 4 + 15 + 10 = 50 cm.

items.q: What is the perimeter of this compound shape?
items.e: Find the missing lengths: 9 − 5 = 4 and 8 − 3 = 5. Then add all 6 sides: 5 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 9 + 8 = 34 m.

items.q: Which statement about rectangles A and B is true?
items.e: Area A = 8 × 3 = 24 cm², area B = 6 × 4 = 24 cm². Perimeter A = 8 + 3 + 8 + 3 = 22 cm, perimeter B = 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 cm. Same area, different perimeters.

items.q: Which statement about rectangles A and B is true?
items.e: Perimeter A = 7 + 2 + 7 + 2 = 18 m, perimeter B = 5 + 4 + 5 + 4 = 18 m. Area A = 7 × 2 = 14 m², area B = 5 × 4 = 20 m². Same perimeter, different areas.

items.q: Rectangle A is 8 cm by 3 cm. Rectangle B has the same area as A and is 6 cm long. What is the perimeter of rectangle B?
items.e: Area of A = 8 × 3 = 24 cm². B: 6 × ? = 24, so B is 4 cm wide. Perimeter of B = 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 cm. Same area does not mean the same perimeter (A has 22 cm).

items.q: Which rectangle has an area of 24 cm² and a perimeter of 20 cm?
items.e: 6 × 4 = 24 cm² and 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 cm. 8 cm by 3 cm has a 22 cm perimeter, 12 cm by 2 cm has 28 cm, and 5 cm by 5 cm has the right perimeter but an area of 25 cm².

items.q: A square has a perimeter of 36 cm. What is its area?
items.e: Each side is 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm. Area = 9 × 9 = 81 cm².

items.q: A square has an area of 64 m². What is its perimeter?
items.e: 8 × 8 = 64, so each side is 8 m. Perimeter = 4 × 8 = 32 m.

items.q: A rectangle has an area of 72 cm². It is 9 cm long. How wide is it?
items.e: Length × width = area, so 9 × ? = 72. 72 ÷ 9 = 8 cm. Check: 9 × 8 = 72.

items.q: What is the area of the right-angled triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the perpendicular height. Area = 12 × 15 × 8 = 12 × 120 = 60 cm². The 17 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the right-angled triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the perpendicular height. Area = 12 × 13 × 12 = 12 × 156 = 78 m².

items.q: What is the area of the right-angled triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the perpendicular height. Area = 12 × 5 × 4 = 12 × 20 = 10 cm².

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?

items.q: A triangle has an area of 36 cm². Its base is 9 cm. What is its perpendicular height?
items.e: 12 × 9 × ? = 36. Double the area first: 36 × 2 = 72. Then 72 ÷ 9 = 8 cm. Check: 12 × 9 × 8 = 12 × 72 = 36 cm².

items.q: A triangle has an area of 42 m². Its perpendicular height is 7 m. What is its base?
items.e: 12 × 7 × ? = 42. Double the area first: 42 × 2 = 84. Then 84 ÷ 7 = 12 m. Check: 12 × 7 × 12 = 12 × 84 = 42 m².

items.q: Which calculation gives the area of the triangle?
items.e: The base is 18 m and the perpendicular height is the dashed 16 m line. Area = 12 × 18 × 16 = 144 m². 18 × 16 forgets to halve, and 34 m is a slanted side.

items.q: Which calculation gives the area of the triangle?
items.e: The base is 28 cm and the perpendicular height is the dashed 24 cm line. Area = 12 × 28 × 24 = 336 cm². 28 × 24 forgets to halve, and 26 cm is a slanted side.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 11 × 12 = 132 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 13 cm side. (Cut the triangle off one end and move it to the other end: you get an 11 by 12 rectangle.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?

items.q: A parallelogram has a base of 8.5 m and a perpendicular height of 6 m. What is its area?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 8.5 × 6 = 51 m². Do not halve: that is only for triangles.

items.q: A parallelogram has a base of 14 cm and a perpendicular height of 11.5 cm. What is its area?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 14 × 11.5 = 161 cm². Do not halve: that is only for triangles.

items.q: A parallelogram has a base of 9 cm, a slanted side of 8 cm and a perpendicular height of 7 cm. What is its area?
items.e: Area = base × perpendicular height = 9 × 7 = 63 cm². The slanted 8 cm side is not used.

items.q: A parallelogram has an area of 96 m². Its base is 12 m. What is its perpendicular height?
items.e: Area = base × height, so 12 × ? = 96. 96 ÷ 12 = 8 m. Check: 12 × 8 = 96.

items.q: A parallelogram has an area of 63 cm². Its perpendicular height is 7 cm. How long is its base?
A parallelogram has an area of 45 cm². Its base is 6 cm. What is its perpendicular height?
items.e: 6 × ? = 45. 45 ÷ 6 = 7.5 cm. Check: 6 × 7.5 = 45. (3.75 cm would be halving, as for a triangle.)

items.q: Which calculation gives the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Base × perpendicular height: 14 × 12 = 168 m². The 13 m side is slanted, and a parallelogram is not halved.

items.q: Which calculation gives the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Base × perpendicular height: 9 × 4 = 36 cm². The 5 cm side is slanted, and a parallelogram is not halved.

items.q: A triangle and a parallelogram both have a base of 10 cm and a perpendicular height of 6 cm. How much greater is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Parallelogram: 10 × 6 = 60 cm². Triangle: 12 × 10 × 6 = 12 × 60 = 30 cm². Difference: 60 − 30 = 30 cm².

items.q: Triangle A has a base of 12 cm and a perpendicular height of 8 cm. Parallelogram B has a base of 6 cm and a perpendicular height of 8 cm. Which is true?
c: A is twice the area of B.
items.e: A: 12 × 12 × 8 = 12 × 96 = 48 cm². B: 6 × 8 = 48 cm². They have the same area. (Forgetting to halve makes A look twice as big.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 13 × 6 = 78 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 10 cm side. (Cut off the triangle on one end and move it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 13 by 6.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 9 × 4 = 36 m². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 5 m side. (Cut off the triangle on one end and move it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 9 by 4.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 7 × 3 = 21 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 5 cm side. (Cut off the triangle on one end and move it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 7 by 3.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 18 × 15 = 270 m². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 17 m side. (Cut off the triangle on one end and move it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 18 by 15.)

items.q: What is the area of the trapezium?
items.e: A = 12 × (b1 + b2) × h = 12 × (16 + 6) × 12 = 12 × 22 × 12 = 132 m². The 13 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the trapezium?
items.e: A = 12 × (b1 + b2) × h = 12 × (19 + 3) × 6 = 12 × 22 × 6 = 66 cm². The 10 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the trapezium?
items.e: A = 12 × (b1 + b2) × h = 12 × (15 + 3) × 8 = 12 × 18 × 8 = 72 m². The 10 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: A parallelogram has a base of 14 cm and a height of 11.5 cm. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height = 14 × 11.5 = 161 cm². No 12 here: a parallelogram is a rectangle with a slanted end moved.

items.q: A trapezium has parallel sides of 12 m and 7.5 m. The distance between them (the height) is 4 m. What is its area?
items.e: A = 12 × (12 + 7.5) × 4 = 12 × 19.5 × 4 = 39 m².

items.q: A parallelogram has an area of 96 m². Its base is 12 m. What is its height?
items.e: Area = base × height, so 12 × ? = 96. 96 ÷ 12 = 8 m. Check: 12 × 8 = 96.

items.q: A trapezium has parallel sides of 7 cm and 13 cm and an area of 60 cm². What is its height?
items.e: 12 × (7 + 13) × h = 60, so 12 × 20 × h = 60, which is 10 × h = 60. h = 60 ÷ 10 = 6 cm. Check: 12 × 20 × 6 = 60.

items.q: Which expression gives the area of the trapezium?
items.e: Add the two parallel sides, multiply by the height (the dashed line), and take half: 12 × (14 + 8) × 4 = 12 × 22 × 4 = 44 m².

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 16 × 15 = 240 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 17 cm side. (Cut off the triangle on one end and move it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 16 by 15.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 15 × 16 = 240 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 20 cm side. (Cut off the triangle on one end and move it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 15 by 16.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 18 × 12 = 216 m². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 15 m side. (Cut off the triangle on one end and move it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 18 by 12.)

items.q: What is the area of the trapezium?
items.e: A = 12 × (b1 + b2) × h = 12 × (26 + 8) × 12 = 12 × 34 × 12 = 204 m². The 15 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the trapezium?
items.e: A = 12 × (b1 + b2) × h = 12 × (16 + 6) × 12 = 12 × 22 × 12 = 132 cm². The 13 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the trapezium?
items.e: A = 12 × (b1 + b2) × h = 12 × (21 + 9) × 8 = 12 × 30 × 8 = 120 m². The 10 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 9 × 4 = 36 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 5 cm side. (Cut off the triangle on one end and move it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 9 by 4.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 16 × 12 = 192 m². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 13 m side. (Cut off the triangle on one end and move it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 16 by 12.)

items.q: The dashed line splits the figure into two rectangles. What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 7 × 7 = 49 and 6 × 3 = 18. Add: 49 + 18 = 67 cm². Use each part of the figure once: 7 × 7 + 13 × 3 = 88 counts the 7 × 3 corner twice.

items.q: The dashed line splits the figure into two rectangles. What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 6 × 7 = 42 and 7 × 4 = 28. Add: 42 + 28 = 70 m². Use each part of the figure once: 6 × 7 + 13 × 4 = 94 counts the 6 × 4 corner twice.

items.q: What is the area of the figure? Find the two missing side lengths first.
items.e: Missing sides: 11 − 6 = 5 and 9 − 5 = 4. Whole rectangle 11 × 9 = 99, minus the missing corner 5 × 4 = 20: 99 − 20 = 79 cm².

items.q: What is the area of the figure? Find the two missing side lengths first.
items.e: Missing sides: 16 − 7 = 9 and 10 − 6 = 4. Whole rectangle 16 × 10 = 160, minus the missing corner 9 × 4 = 36: 160 − 36 = 124 m².

items.q: The figure is a rectangle with a triangle on top. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 16 × 8 = 128 m². Triangle: 12 × 16 × 4 = 12 × 64 = 32 m². Add: 128 + 32 = 160 m².

items.q: The figure is a rectangle with a triangle on top. What is its area?
items.e: The triangle is 12 − 9 = 3 cm tall. Rectangle: 16 × 9 = 144 cm². Triangle: 12 × 16 × 3 = 12 × 48 = 24 cm². Add: 144 + 24 = 168 cm².

items.q: What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Rectangle: 14 × 4 = 56 cm². Triangle: its base is the 4 cm side and its height is 5 cm, so 12 × 4 × 5 = 12 × 20 = 10 cm². Add: 56 + 10 = 66 cm².

items.q: A triangle is cut off the corner of a rectangle (grey dashed lines). What is the area of the shaded figure?
items.e: Whole rectangle: 10 × 8 = 80 cm². Cut-off right triangle: 12 × 3 × 2 = 12 × 6 = 3 cm². Subtract: 80 − 3 = 77 cm².

items.q: A triangle is cut off the corner of a rectangle (grey dashed lines). What is the area of the shaded figure?
items.e: Whole rectangle: 14 × 7 = 98 m². Cut-off right triangle: 12 × 6 × 2 = 12 × 12 = 6 m². Subtract: 98 − 6 = 92 m².

items.q: The dashed line splits the figure into a rectangle and a triangle. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 8 × 8 = 64 cm². The triangle's base is 11 − 8 = 3 cm and its height is 8 cm: 12 × 3 × 8 = 12 × 24 = 12 cm². Add: 64 + 12 = 76 cm².

items.q: The dashed line splits the figure into a rectangle and a triangle. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 10 × 6 = 60 m². The triangle's base is 14 − 10 = 4 m and its height is 6 m: 12 × 4 × 6 = 12 × 24 = 12 m². Add: 60 + 12 = 72 m².

items.q: The hexagon is a rectangle with two equal triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 6 × 8 = 48 m². Each triangle: base 8 m, height 5 m, so 12 × 8 × 5 = 12 × 40 = 20 m². Total: 48 + 20 + 20 = 88 m².

items.q: The dashed line splits the figure into two rectangles. What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 6 × 10 = 60 and 7 × 6 = 42. Add: 60 + 42 = 102 cm². Use each part of the figure once: 6 × 10 + 13 × 6 = 138 counts the 6 × 6 corner twice.

items.q: The dashed line splits the figure into two rectangles. What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 8 × 9 = 72 and 7 × 4 = 28. Add: 72 + 28 = 100 m². Use each part of the figure once: 8 × 9 + 15 × 4 = 132 counts the 8 × 4 corner twice.

items.q: What is the area of the figure? Find the two missing side lengths first.
items.e: Missing sides: 12 − 5 = 7 and 10 − 4 = 6. Whole rectangle 12 × 10 = 120, minus the missing corner 7 × 6 = 42: 120 − 42 = 78 cm².

items.q: What is the area of the figure? Find the two missing side lengths first.
items.e: Missing sides: 9 − 5 = 4 and 7 − 3 = 4. Whole rectangle 9 × 7 = 63, minus the missing corner 4 × 4 = 16: 63 − 16 = 47 m².

items.q: The figure is a rectangle with a triangle on top. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 8 × 4 = 32 m². Triangle: 12 × 8 × 3 = 12 × 24 = 12 m². Add: 32 + 12 = 44 m².

items.q: The figure is a rectangle with a triangle on top. What is its area?
items.e: The triangle is 9 − 4 = 5 cm tall. Rectangle: 10 × 4 = 40 cm². Triangle: 12 × 10 × 5 = 12 × 50 = 25 cm². Add: 40 + 25 = 65 cm².

items.q: What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Rectangle: 12 × 8 = 96 cm². Triangle: its base is the 8 cm side and its height is 8 cm, so 12 × 8 × 8 = 12 × 64 = 32 cm². Add: 96 + 32 = 128 cm².

items.q: A triangle is cut off the corner of a rectangle (grey dashed lines). What is the area of the shaded figure?
items.e: Whole rectangle: 9 × 6 = 54 cm². Cut-off right triangle: 12 × 4 × 3 = 12 × 12 = 6 cm². Subtract: 54 − 6 = 48 cm².
